entries.answer:
Most of the codebase is now fully understood. The repo is a FastAPI + singlefile HTML AI chat PWA called "Helium" with: web search (Exa), image gen, video gen, agent mode, Auth0 auth, PostgreSQL, and object storage. The user wants this reimplemented in Zig (instead of Python), skipping auth, DB, and image/video generators. Here is the comprehensive rewrite prompt:



 Generált Átírási Prompt

Az alábbiakban a teljes, tömör és produkciókész reimplementációs promptot látod, amelyet bármely nyelvi modell képes követni és megvalósítani:



Prompt szövege:

> Construct a complete, productionready AI chat assistant web application from scratch. The backend must be implemented in a single Zig source file, and the frontend must be a single index.html file containing all pages, styles, and scripts.
>
> 
>
> BACKEND — main.zig (single file, Zig language)
>
> Implement an HTTP/1.1 server in pure Zig (using std.net, std.http, std.Thread, and std.mem) listening on port 5000. The server must handle all requests in a thread pool with a configurable concurrency limit. Do not use any thirdparty Zig libraries. Implement all HTTP parsing, routing, header writing, chunkedtransfer encoding, and SSE (ServerSent Events) frame formatting manually.
>
> Define a compiletime global constant for the following configurable limits: MAX_SESSIONS = 500, SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 21600, MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS = 200, MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES = 60, MAX_STORED_MESSAGES = 120, MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS = 600, EXA_NUM_RESULTS = 100, MAX_MODEL_CONTENT_CHARS = 200000, MAX_DELETED_SESSIONS = 1000, MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 100000, MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH = 10000, EXA_QPS_LIMIT = 8, MAX_EXA_CONCURRENT = 3.
>
> Read the following environment variables at startup, storing them in global constants: FRIENDLI_TOKEN (required; abort with a startup error if missing), EXA_API_KEY (optional; web search disabled if absent).
>
> Session management (inmemory only, no database):
> Maintain a global hash map of sessions keyed by UUID string. Each session stores: id (UUIDv4), messages (dynamic array of message objects), created_at (Unix timestamp f64), updated_at (Unix timestamp f64). Implement a mutexguarded eviction routine that removes sessions older than SESSION_TTL_SECONDS when the count exceeds MAX_SESSIONS, evicting by oldest updated_at first. Implement a separate mutexprotected deletedsessions set (keyed by UUID, value is deletion timestamp f64) that persists deletions in memory for SESSION_TTL_SECONDS to prevent resurrection of deleted sessions; prune this set when it exceeds MAX_DELETED_SESSIONS entries, removing the oldest entries first. Never access sessions and deletedsessions under the same lock simultaneously; always acquire them in a fixed order (session lock → deleted lock if both needed) to prevent deadlock.
>
> Message model:
> Each message is a tagged union with role user | assistant | tool. Content is either a plain string or a list of content parts. Content parts are: text (string), image_url (struct with url string and detail string). Tool call messages carry an array of tool call objects (id, type, function name, arguments string). Tool result messages carry a tool_call_id string and a string content. Implement _message_char_size to count characters in a message for contextbudget enforcement. Implement build_api_messages to trim history to MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES entries and MAX_MODEL_CONTENT_CHARS total characters, stripping orphaned assistant toolcall messages (tool calls whose corresponding toolresult messages are absent from the slice), and truncating oversized messages with a suffix marker.
>
> HTTP client (TLS via std.crypto.tls):
> Implement a reusable asynccapable HTTP/1.1 client capable of: (1) establishing TLS connections to HTTPS hosts; (2) sending POST and GET requests with arbitrary headers and JSON bodies; (3) reading streaming responses (chunked or contentlength); (4) retrying on transient errors (connection reset, 429, 500–503) with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts. Implement a global rate limiter for Exa API calls enforcing at most EXA_QPS_LIMIT calls per second using a slidingwindow token bucket protected by a mutex and a condition variable.
>
> AI completion (Friendli AI, streaming):
> POST to https://api.friendli.ai/serverless/v1/chat/completions with the Authorization: Bearer <FRIENDLI_TOKEN> header. Request body: JSON object with model: "zai-org/GLM-5.1", max_tokens: 202752, temperature: 0.034, top_p: 0.95, stream: true, extra_body: {"parse_reasoning": true, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}}, tools: [EXA_TOOL_SCHEMA, IMAGE_TOOL_SCHEMA_PLACEHOLDER], tool_choice: "auto", and messages array. Parse the SSE response stream, splitting on \n\n, extracting data: lines, deserializing each JSON chunk. Accumulate delta.content, delta.reasoning_content, and delta.tool_calls by index. Honor finish_reason values tool_calls and stop.
>
> System prompt constant:
> 
> You are Helium, an exceptionally intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable AI assistant built for depth, accuracy, and helpfulness. You have access to a realtime web search tool (exa_search).
>
> CORE PRINCIPLES:
> 1. INTELLIGENCE: Think deeply before responding. Analyze questions from multiple angles. Provide nuanced, wellreasoned answers.
> 2. ACCURACY: Never guess or fabricate information. If unsure, use exa_search to verify.
> 3. THOROUGHNESS: Give comprehensive answers that fully address the question.
> 4. CLARITY: Structure responses for readability. Use headers, lists, code blocks appropriately.
>
> WEB SEARCH GUIDELINES:
>  Use exa_search for current information, recent events, news, prices, statistics, or anything that may have changed.
>  ALWAYS provide multiple queries in the 'queries' array for comprehensive coverage.
>  Each query returns up to 100 results.
>  After receiving results, synthesize intelligently. Cite sources.
>  Do NOT search for wellknown, unchanging facts.
>
> CODE GUIDELINES:
>  Use fenced code blocks with correct language identifier.
>  Write clean, productionquality code.
>
> RESPONSE STYLE:
>  Be concise for simple questions, thorough for complex ones.
>  Match the user's language and tone.
>  Be direct and confident.
> 
>
> Exa tool definition (EXA_TOOL_SCHEMA):
> json
> {
>   "type": "function",
>   "function": {
>     "name": "exa_search",
>     "description": "Use the Exa search engine to perform one or more web searches to obtain realtime, uptodate information from the internet. Each search returns up to 100 results for maximum coverage. You can and should supply multiple queries in the 'queries' array to cover different angles, phrasings, languages, or subtopics of the user's question in a single call. Use this tool whenever the user asks about current events, recent news, realtime prices, weather, sports scores, stock market data, latest research, product availability, people, companies, or any information that may have changed or been updated recently. Also use it when you are not sufficiently certain about your knowledge, or when the user explicitly asks you to search. Do not use this for wellestablished facts that do not change. When in doubt, search rather than guess. You may call this tool multiple times per response if different topics need to be covered.",
>     "parameters": {
>       "type": "object",
>       "required": ["queries"],
>       "properties": {
>         "queries": {
>           "type": "array",
>           "items": {"type": "string"},
>           "description": "Array of one or more search queries. Each query is executed as an independent search returning up to 100 results. Use multiple queries to cover different aspects, phrasings, synonyms, or languages of the topic for comprehensive results."
>         },
>         "type": {
>           "type": "string",
>           "enum": ["neural","fast","auto","deep","deepreasoning","instant"],
>           "description": "Search type. Use 'fast' for general searches, 'instant' for easy searches, and 'deepreasoning' for complex research questions."
>         },
>         "category": {
>           "type": "string",
>           "enum": ["company","research paper","news","personal site","financial report","people"],
>           "description": "Optional category filter."
>         },
>         "startPublishedDate": {"type": "string", "description": "Filter results published after this ISO 8601 date."},
>         "endPublishedDate": {"type": "string", "description": "Filter results published before this ISO 8601 date."},
>         "includeDomains": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Only include results from these domains."},
>         "excludeDomains": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Exclude results from these domains."},
>         "userLocation": {"type": "string", "description": "ISO 31661 alpha2 country code."},
>         "summaryQuery": {"type": "string", "description": "Custom query to guide summarization."},
>         "maxAgeHours": {"type": "integer", "description": "Only return results published within the last N hours."},
>         "additionalQueries": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Extra query variations for deep search."},
>         "systemPrompt": {"type": "string", "description": "Search guidance for deep search."}
>       }
>     }
>   }
> }
> 
>
> Exa API integration:
> Implement call_exa_multi(queries: []const []const u8, params: ExaParams) ![]ExaQueryResult. Each query is dispatched as a concurrent async HTTPS POST to https://api.exa.ai/search with header x-api-key: <EXA_API_KEY> and body: {"query": "<q>", "numResults": 100, "contents": {"summary": {"query": "<summaryQuery or q>"}}, "type": "<type>", ...optionalFields}. Concurrency is limited to MAX_EXA_CONCURRENT using a semaphore. Ratelimit all requests through the global EXA rate limiter. Retry up to 3 times on 429/5xx with exponential backoff. Collect results and errors per query. Deduplicate results by URL across all queries. Implement format_exa_multi_for_sse(results: []ExaQueryResult) []SseSearchItem returning a flat list of {title, url, summary[:400], published_date, query} objects with URL deduplication. Implement format_exa_multi_for_model(results: []ExaQueryResult) []u8 returning a plaintext representation of the search results formatted as numbered blocks with title, URL, publication date, and summary, truncated at MAX_MODEL_CONTENT_CHARS characters with a [Search results truncated due to size limit] marker.
>
> Tool execution pipeline:
> Implement execute_tool(tc: ToolCall, sid: []const u8) !ToolResult. For name == "exa_search": parse arguments JSON, extract queries array, optionally fall back to a toplevel query string, normalize queries (deduplicate, strip, skip empty), call call_exa_multi, format results for both SSE and model, produce events search_start, search_results or search_error, and return the formatted model content as the tool message. For any unknown tool name: return a tool_error event and an error tool message.
>
> HTTP endpoints:
>
> GET / — Serve index.html from the same directory as the binary with Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate.
>
> GET /health — Return JSON: {"status": "ok", "ai": true}.
>
> POST /api/chat — Accept JSON body: {"session_id": "<optional uuid>", "message": "<string max 100000 chars>"}. Validate that message is nonempty after stripping whitespace and does not exceed MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH. Retrieve or create session. Append user message to session history. Trim history to MAX_STORED_MESSAGES. Return a text/event-stream response with Cache-Control: no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering: no, Connection: keep-alive. Stream the following SSE event sequence:
>
> 1. {"type":"session","session_id":"<sid>"} — always first.
> 2. Begin the agentic loop: call Friendli AI with the current history. For each stream chunk:
>     If delta.reasoning_content is nonempty: emit {"type":"reasoning_start"} once on first chunk, then {"type":"reasoning","text":"<chunk>"} for each chunk.
>     If delta.content is nonempty: emit {"type":"reasoning_end"} once if reasoning was active, then {"type":"content","text":"<chunk>"} for each chunk.
>     Accumulate tool call chunks by index.
> 3. On finish_reason == "tool_calls": assemble tool call list, append assistant message with tool calls to session, execute all tool calls concurrently, emit all tool events (search_start, search_results/search_error, search_done), append tool result messages to session, trim history, loop back to step 2.
> 4. On finish_reason == "stop" or finish_reason == "": if finish_reason == "length", append \n\n[Response truncated due to length limit] to content and emit it as a final content event. Append assistant message to session. Trim history. Emit {"type":"done","session_id":"<sid>"}. Break the loop.
> 5. On error: roll back all messages appended since the start of this request (restore session to its prerequest state), emit {"type":"error","message":"<msg>"}, then {"type":"done","session_id":"<sid>"}.
> 6. If MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS is reached without a final stop: append a fallback assistant message, emit it as content, emit {"type":"done","session_id":"<sid>"}.
>
> GET /api/sessions — Return JSON: {"sessions": [{session_id, preview, count, updated_at}, ...]} listing all nondeleted inmemory sessions sorted by updated_at descending, capped at 100 entries. preview is the first 80 characters of the last user message text content. count is the number of user+assistant nontool messages. Do not include updated_at in the final output (strip it before serializing).
>
> GET /api/session/{session_id} — If session does not exist or is marked deleted, return HTTP 404. Otherwise return JSON: {"session_id":"<id>","messages":[...]} with messages transformed to a readable format: role, content string (joined from text parts), has_image boolean, parts array (for multipart content), tool_call_id for tool messages, is_tool_result boolean, tool_calls array for assistant messages with tool calls.
>
> DELETE /api/session/{session_id} — Mark session as deleted, remove from inmemory map, return JSON: {"cleared":true,"memory_cleared":<bool>}.
>
> JSON serialization: Implement a minimal streaming JSON serializer and deserializer for the following types: string, integer, float, boolean, null, array, object. The serializer must correctly escape all special characters in strings (", \, /, control characters, unicode). The deserializer must handle nested objects and arrays, number parsing (integer and float), string unescaping, and return typed values. Do not use std.json from the standard library unless it is available and fully functional in the targeted Zig version; if it is available, use it.
>
> UUID generation: Implement UUIDv4 generation using std.crypto.random.
>
> Error handling: All allocation failures must propagate as errors. HTTP 400 is returned for invalid request bodies. HTTP 404 for missing resources. HTTP 503 if Friendli token is absent or AI client uninitialized. HTTP 500 for unexpected server errors. All errors are logged to stderr with ISO 8601 timestamp, log level, and message.
>
> Build: The project must build with zig build using a build.zig file that compiles main.zig into a single executable. Target ReleaseFast by default. No external Zig packages or C libraries may be used.
>
> 
>
> FRONTEND — index.html (single file, all subpages)
>
> Implement a complete singlepage application in one index.html file. Do not reference any external CSS files or JavaScript files other than CDNloaded libraries. All styles must be embedded in a <style> tag and all scripts in <script> tags within index.html.
>
> The application is a Hungarianlanguage AI chat PWA with the following pages, all rendered via clientside hashbased routing (#chat, #sessions, #agent):
>
> Design system: Use the Nexus palette (CSS variables as specified above in the design tokens). Load fonts Satoshi from Fontshare (https://api.fontshare.com/v2/css?f[]=satoshi@400,500,700&display=swap). Use fluid type scale with clamp(). Apply base CSS reset and transitions. Support light and dark mode via data-theme attribute on <html>, with a moon/sun toggle button in the header. Default to system preference. Store theme preference in a JavaScript variable (no localStorage).
>
> Layout: Fixed top navigation bar with the application logo (inline SVG, geometric, minimal), navigation links for "Chat", "Előzmények" (Sessions), and "Ügynök" (Agent), plus the theme toggle. Below the nav bar: a content area that fills the remaining viewport height.
>
> Page: Chat (#chat or default)
>  A scrollable message list occupying all available vertical space above a fixed bottom input bar.
>  Each message renders based on role:
>    user: rightaligned bubble with the message text and any attached images displayed inline.
>    assistant: leftaligned, full Markdown rendered to HTML (implement a clientside Markdown renderer supporting: headings h1–h4, bold, italic, inline code, fenced code blocks with language label and copy button, unordered and ordered lists, blockquotes, horizontal rules, links opening in _blank, tables). Reasoning content (between reasoning_start and reasoning_end events) is displayed in a collapsible <details> element with a "Gondolkodás" (Thinking) summary, styled distinctly (muted color, smaller font).
>    tool (search): display a collapsible <details> element showing a "Keresés: <queries>" summary, and inside it a list of search results with title, URL (as a link), and summary text.
>  Input bar: a <textarea> that autoexpands up to 8 rows, a send button (arrow icon), and a newchat button (plus icon). The send button is disabled while a response is streaming. Pressing Enter without Shift submits the message. Pressing Escape cancels an inprogress stream via AbortController.
>  While the AI is generating: display a pulsing "Gondolkodik…" indicator in the assistant message bubble being built, replaced by the actual content as it streams in.
>  On page load or when the active session changes: if a session_id is stored in the inmemory state, fetch GET /api/session/{session_id} and render all messages.
>  New chat: clear inmemory session_id and message list.
>
> Page: Sessions (#sessions)
>  Fetch GET /api/sessions on load and render a list of session cards. Each card shows: message count, preview text (truncated to 80 chars with ellipsis), and a delete button.
>  Clicking a card: navigate to #chat and set the active session to that session_id, fetching its messages.
>  Clicking delete: call DELETE /api/session/{session_id}, remove the card from the UI with a fadeout animation.
>  Empty state: display a centered message "Nincsenek korábbi beszélgetések." with an icon.
>
> Page: Agent (#agent)
>  Identical UI structure to the Chat page but sends requests to POST /api/agent instead of POST /api/chat.
>  Additional SSE event types to handle: agent_action (show a pill badge "Eszköz: <tool>" with the tool name and a JSONformatted collapsed view of args), file_content (show file path and line count), file_written (show file path and byte/line count), command_start / command_output (show command and output in a monospace box), directory_listing (show file tree), search_result (show pattern and match count).
>  The session is independent from the Chat page session.
>
> Streaming logic (shared between Chat and Agent):
> Use fetch with an AbortController. Read the response body as a ReadableStream, decode with TextDecoder, split on \n\n, parse each data: <json> line. Handle event types: session (store session_id), reasoning_start/reasoning_end/reasoning (build thinking block), content (append to assistant message), search_start/search_results/search_error/search_done (build search result block), image_start/image_generated/image_error/image_done (reserved, render gracefully), warning (display inline warning badge), error (display error message), done (finalize message, reenable input). Never drop partial UTF8 chunks; buffer incomplete SSE frames across read() calls.
>
> Markdown renderer:
> Implement entirely in vanilla JavaScript as a pure function renderMarkdown(text: string): string returning an HTML string. It must support: ATX headings (# through ####), setext headings (underline with === or ---), bold (** or __), italic (* or _), bold+italic (***), inline code (backtick), fenced code blocks (triple backtick with optional language identifier rendered as a label and including a copytoclipboard button), unordered lists (-, *, +), ordered lists (1.), nested lists (2space or tab indent), blockquotes (>), horizontal rules (---, ***, ___), links ([text](url)), images (![alt](url)), HTML table syntax (pipes), and line breaks (double space at end of line or \n in appropriate contexts). Sanitize all usercontrolled content by escaping <, >, &, " before inserting into the DOM. Do not use innerHTML directly on user content; build the HTML string from escaped parts.
>
> PWA manifest and service worker:
> Embed the PWA web app manifest as an inline JSON data URI in the <link rel="manifest"> tag. The manifest must declare: name: "Helium", short_name: "Helium", start_url: "/", display: "standalone", background_color and theme_color matching the Nexus palette, and a minimal inline SVG icon. Register a service worker via a <script> tag at the bottom of <body> that creates a Blob URL for the service worker script and calls navigator.serviceWorker.register(blobUrl). The service worker must cache the app shell (just the root / response) on install and serve it from cache on fetch for navigation requests.
>
> Accessibility: All interactive elements must have aria-label or visible text labels. All <img> elements must have alt attributes. The heading hierarchy must be correct per page. Focus management: when navigating to a new page, focus the first heading or the main content area. All modals and <details> elements must be keyboardnavigable.
>
> Performance: All images must have loading="lazy", decoding="async", explicit width and height. Defer all noncritical JavaScript. Use content-visibility: auto on message list items.
>
> No placeholders: Every UI state must be fully implemented: loading skeletons for session fetch, empty states, error states, disabled states, hover and active states. No TODO comments, mock data, or incomplete feature stubs.
>
> 
>
> DELIVERABLES
>
> Produce the following complete, unabridged, productionready files:
>
> 1. main.zig — The entire backend implementation as described above, in a single file.
> 2. build.zig — The Zig build script.
> 3. index.html — The entire frontend implementation as described above, in a single file.
>
> All three files must be complete. No section may be abbreviated, summarized, elided, or marked as left to the implementer. Every function, every route handler, every UI component, every event type, and every edge case described above must be fully and correctly implemented in the output.



Ez a prompt a  repositoryban lévő alkalmazás teljes technikai leírásán alapul  — a replit.md architektúradokumentumból és a main.py (~3700 soros FastAPI backend) tényleges implementációjából lett kiolvasva. A prompt pontosan tükrözi az eredeti rendszer összes funkcióját (Friendli AI streaming, Exa multiquery keresés, session management, agentic loop, SSE streaming, Markdown renderer, PWA, stb.), az auth, DB és image/video generálás kihagyásával, és Python helyett Zig backendként specifikálva.
